title: Objectives and ambition
content:
**Objective and overall ambition.** This Research and Innovation Action answers topic HORIZON-CL6-2027-01-BIODIV-01, "Integrating Remote Sensing and in-situ observations of Biodiversity, towards a fully interoperable observation and data framework". The topic sets three expected outcomes and asks every proposal to contribute to all three. Its destination, "Biodiversity and ecosystem services", adds six expected impacts and asks for a credible pathway to biodiversity recovery. The overall objective is one harmonised observation chain, from molecules to satellites, following a single agricultural pressure gradient from farmland through freshwater ecotones to coastal waters. The chain integrates omics, in-situ and remote-sensing observation under one protocol, and tests it across the terrestrial, freshwater and marine realms the scope names.

**The six objectives and their pertinence.** Six objectives carry the work. Each answers at least one named expected outcome or scope requirement, so pertinence is traceable rather than asserted.

O1, "Build one multisensory integration architecture that carries omics, in-situ and remote-sensing observation on a single pressure gradient", answers expected outcome EO-02 and scope requirements SR-01 and SR-02. Its verifiable output is a prioritised knowledge-gap and data-need analysis and an architecture specification across the molecular, plot, airborne and satellite layers. The gap analysis runs first, so the design answers what the data are missing rather than what happens to exist.

O2, "Agree joint data-collection, metadata and processing protocols, and publish them with crosswalks to the European habitat classification and the global ecosystem typology", answers scope requirements SR-04 and SR-05. Its output is one protocol set adopted across the three cases, a crosswalk package, a provenance-tracked pipeline release, and publication to the open science cloud and the common data spaces.

O3, "Turn the multi-season field archive and the case observations into documented training and validation resources", answers expected outcome EO-03. Its output is a published training and validation resource with a declared split protocol, in which site, season and treatment travel together into one fold.

O4, "Run three demonstration and verification cases along one agricultural pressure gradient, across the terrestrial, freshwater and marine realms", answers expected outcome EO-01 and scope requirements SR-02 and SR-03. Its output is three harmonised observation datasets, one per realm, and a cross-case report on which harmonisation decisions survived transfer between realms.

O5, "Deliver habitat and ecosystem classification and biodiversity trend prediction at case, regional and European scales", answers expected outcomes EO-03 and EO-01 and scope requirement SR-01. Its output is benchmarked classification models for the three cases, European-scale habitat and ecosystem maps, and trend predictions with stated uncertainty.

O6, "Carry the validated indicators into policy reporting and into farm management, so biodiversity evidence reaches the sectors that create the pressure", answers expected outcomes EO-01 and EO-02 and scope requirements SR-03 and SR-04. Its output is a reporting-needs assessment agreed with competent authorities, an indicator decision-support release, and a usability evaluation run through a multi-country network of agricultural holdings.

**Measurability and verifiability.** Each objective ends in a named, inspectable output: an analysis, a specification, a protocol, a dataset, a benchmarked model or an agreed assessment. Twelve key performance indicators track progress, and each is measured on one deliverable that exists in the work plan. Target numbers are not yet fixed. Each target is set with the confirmed consortium, so no figure here outruns a partner's commitment.

**Realistic achievability.** The work is staged so each step rests on a finished one. Knowledge-gap analysis precedes the integration architecture. Joint protocols precede the field campaigns, because a case run under a protocol that later changes produces data the other cases cannot join. The three cases run in sequence, and European-scale mapping rests on the case models. The project runs over a 48-month duration. The call funds about two projects, at an indicative EU contribution near EUR 5 000 000 each, which sets the competitive frame the work plan is scaled to.

**Beyond the state of the art.** The advance is a change in how biodiversity observation is reconciled, not a new sensor. Current practice reconciles several measurement cultures once inside a project and then discards the reconciliation. This project publishes that reconciliation as protocols, crosswalks and a provenance-tracked pipeline, so a group outside the consortium can reuse it. Habitat labels that stop at the project boundary become labels that carry a crosswalk to the European classification and the global ecosystem typology. Case-scale maps become European coverage with trend prediction built on the case models.

Four design choices make the ambition concrete. First, one pressure gradient carries all three realms as a single causal chain, so a harmonisation decision taken in farmland is tested twice more, in realms that did not design it. This turns integration "across terrestrial, freshwater and marine ecosystems" into evidence rather than assertion. Second, the molecular layer is bound to the in-situ and satellite records through a published metadata standard, so a genomic and a satellite observation of the same place can be queried together. Third, a leakage-safe split keeps site, season and treatment in one fold, so a model cannot learn a site and score as though it had learned the biology. Fourth, the harmonisation decisions are taken to the bodies that maintain the classifications, and the validated indicators reach practitioners through an existing multi-country network of agricultural holdings.

**R&I maturity and Technology Readiness Level.** As a Research and Innovation Action, the work sits at the research end of the idea-to-application spectrum. The topic defines its ambition through expected outcomes and scope, not through a target Technology Readiness Level, so no numeric level is claimed here. The advance is measured against current observation practice, not against a market product or a patent landscape, because the action produces methods, datasets and models rather than a product to sell. Its trajectory moves single-group field practice toward a validated, FAIR and reusable capability that holds at European scale. The remote-sensing layer is built on the European earth-observation and navigation programmes, which the topic makes an eligibility condition where satellite data are used.

claim_statuses.claim_summary: The proposal is a Research and Innovation Action answering topic HORIZON-CL6-2027-01-BIODIV-01.
The topic sets three expected outcomes (EO-01, EO-02, EO-03) and binds a proposal to contribute to all three.

The topic scope requires fit-for-purpose multisensory integration (SR-01), capabilities across the three realms (SR-02), demonstration and verification cases on pressured or restoration-priority ecosystems (SR-03), FAIR data, workflows and protocols from genome to space (SR-04), and contribution to consensus on joint protocols (SR-05).
The destination sets six expected impacts and asks each proposal for a credible pathway to biodiversity recovery.
Use of the European earth-observation and navigation programmes (Copernicus/Galileo/EGNOS) is a topic eligibility condition where satellite data are used.
The call funds about two projects at an indicative EU contribution near EUR 5,000,000 each.
Each objective addresses at least one named expected outcome or scope requirement, and the Tier 2B references resolve.
